title: Weak saturation under Cartesian pushout product
statement:
Use small simplicial sets and degreewise products of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] and colimits of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. A monomorphism means a degreewise injective map. Call a class of maps weakly saturated if it contains all isomorphisms and is closed under pushouts, small transfinite compositions and retracts in the category of maps. Here a transfinite composition is the composite of a small ordinal-indexed chain which is a colimit of its earlier stages at each nonzero limit ordinal. A retract in the category of maps is given by commutative section and retraction squares whose composite is the identity square. Let $W$ be any weakly saturated class of simplicial maps. For monomorphisms $i:A\hookrightarrow B$ and $k:K\hookrightarrow L$, let $\theta_{i,k}$ be the canonical map
$$ (A\times L)\amalg_{A\times K}(B\times K)\longrightarrow B\times L. $$
For each fixed monomorphism $k$, the class of monomorphisms $i$ such that $\theta_{i,k}\in W$ is weakly saturated. For each fixed monomorphism $i$, the class of monomorphisms $k$ such that $\theta_{i,k}\in W$ is weakly saturated.

source.place: Proposition 4.2.5.3 (0153), proof: the weak saturation of T for fixed second variable and of T-prime for fixed first variable; generalized here from the right-anodyne class to an arbitrary weakly saturated W. Kerodon tag, not the unrelated Stacks tag; read online, archival copy WANTED in report.md.

proof.text: Identify each monomorphism with its degreewise image inclusion. In each simplicial degree the domain of $\theta_{i,k}$ is the union $(A\times L)\cup(B\times K)$ inside $B\times L$, and the intersection is $A\times K$; hence the displayed map is the pushout inclusion. Products and these unions are preserved by every simplicial operator, so this degreewise identification is simplicial. Commutative squares in either input induce commutative squares of $\theta$-maps, preserving identities and composition. In particular, section and retraction squares in either variable induce section and retraction squares of the corresponding $\theta$-maps.

source.place: Proposition 4.2.5.3, degreewise construction and functoriality of the Cartesian pushout product.

proof.text: Fix a monomorphism $k:K\hookrightarrow L$ and let $T_k$ be the class of monomorphisms $i$ for which $\theta_{i,k}$ belongs to $W$. If $i$ is an isomorphism, then the union in Step 1 is all of $B\times L$, so $\theta_{i,k}$ is an isomorphism and belongs to $W$. Thus $T_k$ contains all isomorphisms.

source.place: Proposition 4.2.5.3, proof of the weak-saturation assertion for fixed $k$, isomorphism case.

proof.text: Suppose $i_0:A_0\hookrightarrow B_0$ lies in $T_k$ and form a pushout $i':A'\to B'=B_0\amalg_{A_0}A'$ along an arbitrary, possibly non-injective, map $g:A_0\to A'$. Degreewise, $B'$ is the quotient of $A'\amalg B_0$ identifying each $a\in A_0$ with $g(a)$; since $i_0$ is injective, $B'$ is the disjoint union of $A'$ and $B_0\setminus A_0$, so $i'$ is again a monomorphism. Write $D_0=(A_0\times L)\cup(B_0\times K)\subseteq B_0\times L$ and $D'=(A'\times L)\cup(B'\times K)\subseteq B'\times L$ (Step 1). Consider the commutative square with top $D_0\to D'$ induced by $g$ and $B_0\to B'$, left side $\theta_{i_0,k}:D_0\hookrightarrow B_0\times L$, right side $\theta_{i',k}:D'\hookrightarrow B'\times L$ and bottom $B_0\times L\to B'\times L$. In each degree the left side is injective, so the pushout of $D'\leftarrow D_0\hookrightarrow B_0\times L$ is $D'$ disjoint union the complement $(B_0\times L)\setminus D_0=(B_0\setminus A_0)\times(L\setminus K)$. The complement of $D'$ in $B'\times L=(A'\amalg(B_0\setminus A_0))\times L$ is also $(B_0\setminus A_0)\times(L\setminus K)$, and the bottom map is the identity on it; hence the canonical map from that pushout to $B'\times L$ is bijective in each degree. Since colimits of simplicial sets are computed degreewise, the square is a pushout. Hence $\theta_{i',k}$ lies in $W$ by pushout closure, so $T_k$ is closed under pushouts.

source.place: Proposition 4.2.5.3, proof of closure of $T$ under pushouts.

proof.text: Let $(X_\alpha)_{\alpha\leq\lambda}$ be a continuous ordinal chain of monomorphisms in $T_k$. Degreewise, a chain of injective maps has injective maps into its colimit (two elements become equal only after a later transition identifies them, which cannot happen for injections), so after replacing each stage by its image we may regard it as nested simplicial subsets of $X_\lambda$. Put $P_\alpha=(X_\alpha\times L)\cup(X_\lambda\times K)$ inside $X_\lambda\times L$. For each $\alpha<\lambda$, put $E_\alpha=(X_\alpha\times L)\cup(X_{\alpha+1}\times K)$. Directly degreewise, $P_\alpha\cap(X_{\alpha+1}\times L)=E_\alpha$ and $P_\alpha\cup(X_{\alpha+1}\times L)=P_{\alpha+1}$, so $P_\alpha\to P_{\alpha+1}$ is a pushout of $\theta_{X_\alpha\hookrightarrow X_{\alpha+1},k}$ and belongs to $W$.

source.place: Proposition 4.2.5.3, proof of closure of $T$ under transfinite compositions, successor stages.

proof.text: At every nonzero limit ordinal $\delta$, every simplex of $X_\delta$ lies in some earlier $X_\alpha$, so the union formula gives $P_\delta=\bigcup_{\alpha<\delta}P_\alpha$. Hence the chain $(P_\alpha)_{\alpha\leq\lambda}$ is continuous; it starts at $P_0=(X_0\times L)\cup(X_\lambda\times K)$, the domain of $\theta_{X_0\hookrightarrow X_\lambda,k}$, and ends at $P_\lambda=X_\lambda\times L$, its codomain, and its composite $P_0\hookrightarrow P_\lambda$ is $\theta_{X_0\hookrightarrow X_\lambda,k}$. The composite $X_0\to X_\lambda$ is a monomorphism by Step 4. Closure of $W$ under transfinite compositions makes $\theta_{X_0\hookrightarrow X_\lambda,k}$ lie in $W$; the zero-length chain is the isomorphism case. Therefore $T_k$ is closed under transfinite compositions.

source.place: Proposition 4.2.5.3, proof of closure of $T$ under transfinite compositions, limit stages.

proof.text: Let $i:A\to B$ be a retract of $j:A''\hookrightarrow B''$ in $T_k$ in the category of maps, with section maps $a:A\to A''$, $b:B\to B''$ and retraction maps $r:A''\to A$, $s:B''\to B$, $ra=1_A$. Then $i$ is a monomorphism: if $i(x)=i(y)$ then $j(a(x))=b(i(x))=b(i(y))=j(a(y))$, so $a(x)=a(y)$ and $x=ra(x)=ra(y)=y$, degreewise. By Step 1 the section and retraction squares induce a section and retraction of $\theta_{i,k}$ from $\theta_{j,k}$. Since $W$ is closed under retracts, membership of $\theta_{j,k}$ in $W$ implies membership of $\theta_{i,k}$. Thus $T_k$ is closed under retracts. Together with Steps 2--5, $T_k$ is weakly saturated.

source.place: Proposition 4.2.5.3, proof of closure of $T$ under retracts and conclusion for fixed $k$.

proof.text: Now fix a monomorphism $i:A\hookrightarrow B$ and let $T_i'$ be the class of monomorphisms $k$ for which $\theta_{i,k}$ belongs to $W$. The same degreewise union argument as in Step 1 shows that isomorphisms in the second variable give isomorphisms $\theta_{i,k}$, hence $T_i'$ contains all isomorphisms.

source.place: Proposition 4.2.5.3, proof of the weak-saturation assertion for fixed $i$, isomorphism case.

proof.text: Let $k_0:K_0\hookrightarrow L_0$ lie in $T_i'$ and let $k':K'\to L'=L_0\amalg_{K_0}K'$ be its pushout along an arbitrary, possibly non-injective, map $K_0\to K'$. Degreewise, $L'$ is the quotient of $K'\amalg L_0$ identifying each element of $K_0$ with its image in $K'$; since $k_0$ is injective, $L'$ is the disjoint union of $K'$ and $L_0\setminus K_0$, so $k'$ is a monomorphism. Write $D_0=(A\times L_0)\cup(B\times K_0)\subseteq B\times L_0$ and $D'=(A\times L')\cup(B\times K')\subseteq B\times L'$, and consider the square with top $D_0\to D'$, left side $\theta_{i,k_0}$, right side $\theta_{i,k'}$ and bottom $B\times L_0\to B\times L'$. Since the left side is injective in each degree, its pushout is $D'$ disjoint union $(B\times L_0)\setminus D_0=(B\setminus A)\times(L_0\setminus K_0)$, which is exactly the complement of $D'$ in $B\times L'=B\times(K'\amalg(L_0\setminus K_0))$, with the bottom map the identity there. Hence the square is a degreewise, so simplicial, pushout. Pushout closure of $W$ gives $\theta_{i,k'}\in W$, so $T_i'$ is closed under pushouts.

source.place: Proposition 4.2.5.3, proof of closure of $T'$ under pushouts.

proof.text: For a continuous ordinal chain $(Y_\alpha)_{\alpha\leq\lambda}$ in $T_i'$, the same degreewise injectivity argument as in Step 4 shows that $Y_0\to Y_\lambda$ is a monomorphism and lets us represent the stages as nested subsets of $Y_\lambda$. Put $Q_\alpha=(B\times Y_\alpha)\cup(A\times Y_\lambda)$. The same intersection and union calculation gives that each successor $Q_\alpha\to Q_{\alpha+1}$ is a pushout of $\theta_{i,Y_\alpha\hookrightarrow Y_{\alpha+1}}$, while at a limit $Q_\delta=\bigcup_{\alpha<\delta}Q_\alpha$. Transfinite-composition closure of $W$ therefore puts $\theta_{i,Y_0\hookrightarrow Y_\lambda}$ in $W$; the zero-length case is an isomorphism.

source.place: Proposition 4.2.5.3, proof of closure of $T'$ under transfinite compositions.

proof.text: If $k$ is a retract of $l\in T_i'$ in the category of maps, then $k$ is a monomorphism by the same degreewise computation as in Step 6, and Step 1 makes $\theta_{i,k}$ a retract of $\theta_{i,l}$. Retract closure of $W$ gives $\theta_{i,k}\in W$. Thus $T_i'$ is closed under retracts, and Steps 7--10 show that it is weakly saturated.

source.place: Proposition 4.2.5.3, proof of closure of $T'$ under retracts and conclusion for fixed $i$.
